motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Routine consent items approved in one vote
motions.summary: The council passed its consent agenda, the batch of routine items voted through together; this record doesn't list which items were included.
motions.impact: Consent agendas hold the routine business the council doesn't debate individually. Nothing in this record points to a change residents would notice.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Approving the Second Amendment to the Fiscal Year 2025 - 2026 Annual Budget as presented
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Approving the Second Amendment to the Fiscal Year 2025 - 2026 Annual Budget as presented . Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Mid-year change to this year's city budget
motions.summary: The council approved a second amendment to the 2025–26 city budget, adopted as presented; the motion lists no figures or specific changes.
motions.impact: A mid-year budget amendment can move real money, but this record doesn't say what changed. To see whether anything you use is affected, you'd need the budget document itself.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the Issuance and Sale of Not More Than $220,000,000 Aggregate Principal Amount of Water and Sewer Revenue Bonds, Series 2026; Fixing the Maximum Aggregate Principal Amount of the Bonds; Th e Maximum Number of Years Over Which the Bonds May Mature, the Maximum Interest Rate Which the Bonds May Bear, and the Maximum Discount From Par at Which the Bonds May be Sold; Providing for the Publication of a Notice of Public Hearing and Bonds to be Iss ued; Providing for the Running of a Contest Period; Authorizing the Execution by the City of a General and Supplemental Indenture of Trust, and Other Documents Necessary for the Issuance of the Series 2026 Bonds; Authorizing the Taking of All Other Actions Necessary to the Consummation of the Transaction Contemplated by this Resolution; and Related Matters.
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the Issuance and Sale of Not More Than $230,000,000 Aggregate Principal Amount of Water and Sewer Revenue Bonds, Series 2026; as presented in the agenda. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Up to $220M in water and sewer bonds
motions.summary: The city authorized borrowing up to $220 million — the motion as read said $230 million — by selling water and sewer revenue bonds.
motions.impact: Before the bonds are sold, the city must publish notice of a public hearing and allow a window in which the sale can be legally challenged. Revenue bonds are repaid from water and sewer bills, not property taxes.

motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 15.95 and Eagle Mountain City CouMnicnilu te –s February 1, 72026 Page9 of 12 Adopting the Eagle Mountain City Wildland Urban Interface Area Map. Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New wildfire-risk map for homes next to open land
motions.summary: The city adopted an official Wildland Urban Interface map — the areas where homes back onto undeveloped wildland — and amended the related section of city code.
motions.impact: If your property backs onto open land, it may now fall inside the mapped interface area. The motion doesn't spell out what rules come with that.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing Chapter 2.30 (Parks and Recreation Advisory Board), Chapter 2.40 (Recreation Sports Board), Chapter 2.55 (Cemetery Board), Chapter 2.60 (Military and Veterans Advisory Board), and Chapter 2.7 0 (Economic Development Board) and Enacting Chapter 2.80 of the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code to Establish a Community Services Board.
motions.motion: Councilmember Huish moved to adopt a n Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing Chapter 2.30 (Parks and Recreation Advisory Board), Chapter 2.40 (Recreation Sports Board), Chapter 2.55 (Cemetery Board), Chapter 2.60 (Military and Veterans Advisory Board), and Chapter 2.70 (Economic D evelopment Board) and Enacting Chapter 2.80 of the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code to Establish a Community Services Board. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Merge five city boards into one
motions.summary: The council considered folding the parks, recreation sports, cemetery, veterans, and economic development boards into a single Community Services Board.
motions.impact: If you volunteer on one of those five boards, they would be replaced by one combined board. For everyone else, nothing changes day to day.
